Hi Sarah,

Thanks for the call earlier. We saw the late completions on a few of your bulk inference jobs this past weekend (batch job ids attached). The runs exceeded the current 30-minute completion window and in one case retried from the queue which resulted in duplicate downstream records.

We'd like to propose a short-term commercial and technical remediation so you avoid production disruption while we roll out the idempotency/dedup changes on your Dedicated pool:

- Contract: a temporary extension of the "job completion window" from 30 minutes to 2 hours for your "bulk-import" job type for up to 30 days (we'll log incidents and provide weekly reports).
- Commercial: one-time usage credit for impacted runs while mitigation is in progress.
- Technical: recommended changes (idempotency keys, incremental checkpointing, heartbeat + lease model, and at-least-once with dedupe on ingestion). See attached samples and logs.

Can we confirm (a) that Acme accepts the 30-day remediation window, and (b) that your team can make a small consumer-side change to honor idempotency keys we will emit?

If you approve, I will loop in Dev for a technical runbook and Karthik to align on contract amendment and credits.

Best,

Rachel Kim

On Mon, May 18, 2026 at 9:46 AM Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com> wrote:
> Thanks Rachel — appreciate the quick follow-up. We observed two customer-facing incidents where the bulk import finished late and some records were processed twice (customers noticed duplicate IDs).

Hi all,

Short technical summary and concrete mitigations we can deliver quickly:

1) Semantics: we currently operate with at-least-once delivery for async batch jobs. That means retries can produce duplicates unless consumers dedupe. We cannot flip to exactly-once without end-to-end changes.

2) Immediate mitigations (2–7 days):
   - Emit idempotency_key for each input item: <job_id>::<input_index>::<sha1(input_payload)>
   - Store last-processed-key in the output ledger (S3/DB) and surface in job metadata. Consumers can check and ignore duplicates.
   - Checkpointing: stream partial results to a job-output prefix so long-running jobs can resume from last checkpoint.
   - Heartbeat + lease: jobs will renew a short-lived lease; if we detect a stuck worker we will requeue remaining segments with the same job id and keys.

3) Retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter, capped retries per segment (configurable). We will flag segments that hit the retry cap and provide a partial-completion artifact.

4) Operational monitoring: we'll add a per-job page with the following endpoints (examples):
   - /jobs/{job_id}/status — current state and last heartbeat
   - /jobs/{job_id}/artifacts — s3 prefix for partial outputs
   - /jobs/{job_id}/retries — failure and retry counts

5) Migration timeline: deploy idempotency headers and partial-output streaming to your Dedicated pool within 10 business days. During that period we recommend the 30-day completion window extension so we can avoid false SLA breaches.

Example idempotency key pseudo:
   job_id = "acme-bulk-20260516-09"
   for i, item in enumerate(batch):
       key = f"{job_id}:{i}:{sha1(item)}"
       emit(item, idempotency_key=key)

We can also provide a small sample consumer script to ignore duplicates based on the key.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

- Credit: one-time credit equal to the impacted token usage for incidents logged between 2026-05-15 and 2026-05-18 (we'll share a usage CSV).
- Post-remediation: if the idempotency rollout completes and incident rate is below the agreed threshold, we revert to standard SLA.

We need Stephanie (legal/CS) to prepare a short amendment and confirm approval flow. Karthik (me) will own the credit calculation and accounting entry. Rachel will own customer sign-off and weekly syncs.
